question: Which cranial nerve is responsible for taste sensation in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue?
explanation:
• The Facial nerve (VII) via the chorda tympani branch carries taste sensation from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue.
• Glossopharyngeal (IX) carries taste from the posterior 1/3. Frequently asked in RRB Nursing (2022, 2024).

question: What is the normal pH range of blood?
explanation:
• Normal arterial blood pH is 7.35–7.45. Below 7.35 is acidosis; above 7.45 is alkalosis.
• Homeostasis is maintained by buffers, lungs, and kidneys.

question: Which chamber of the heart receives deoxygenated blood from the body?
explanation:
• Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from superior and inferior vena cava.
• Blood then flows to right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs for oxygenation.

question: Where does gas exchange occur in the respiratory system?
explanation:
• Gas exchange (O2 and CO2) occurs in the alveoli due to large surface area and thin walls.
• Alveoli are the functional units of the lungs.

question: Which hormone is produced by the adrenal medulla?
explanation:
• Adrenal medulla secretes epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine (fight-or-flight).
• Cortisol and aldosterone are from the adrenal cortex.

question: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
explanation:
• The nephron is the functional unit; it filters blood and forms urine.
• Each kidney has about 1 million nephrons.

question: Which blood type is the universal donor?
explanation:
• O negative has no A, B, or Rh antigens, so it can be given to any recipient in emergencies.
• AB positive is the universal recipient.

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves are there?
explanation:
• There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves (I–XII).
• They arise from the brain and supply the head, neck, and some visceral structures.

question: Which organ is the primary site of glycogen storage?
explanation:
• Liver stores glycogen and releases glucose when needed (glycogenolysis).
• Muscle also stores glycogen for local use.

question: Which structure connects the two cerebral hemispheres?
explanation:
• Corpus callosum is a band of nerve fibers connecting left and right cerebral hemispheres.
• It allows communication between the two sides of the brain.

question: Normal adult hemoglobin range (g/dL) for males is approximately:
explanation:
• Adult males: 14-17 g/dL; adult females: 12-15 g/dL.
• Below normal indicates anemia. Often asked in RRB Nursing (2022, 2024).

question: Which valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle?
explanation:
• Mitral (bicuspid) valve is between left atrium and left ventricle.
• Tricuspid is right atrium to right ventricle.

question: The sinoatrial (SA) node is located in:
explanation:
• SA node in right atrium is the natural pacemaker (initiates heartbeat).
• AV node is in interatrial septum.

question: Normal adult respiratory rate per minute is:
explanation:
• Normal adult: 12-20 breaths/min. Tachypnea >20; bradypnea <12.
• Part of vital signs in nursing assessment.

question: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
explanation:
• Cerebellum coordinates voluntary movement, balance, posture.
• Medulla controls vital functions (respiration, heart rate).

question: Insulin is secreted by:
explanation:
• Beta cells of islets of Langerhans secrete insulin (lowers blood glucose).
• Alpha cells secrete glucagon.

question: Largest organ of the human body is:
explanation:
• Skin is the largest organ (by surface area and weight).
• Liver is the largest internal organ.

question: Number of bones in adult human body is approximately:
explanation:
• Adult human has 206 bones. Infant has more (some fuse later).
• Commonly asked in RRB/paramedical exams.

question: Which electrolyte is primarily intracellular (highest inside the cell)?
explanation:
• Potassium (K+) is the main intracellular cation. Sodium (Na+) is main extracellular.
• Critical for nerve and muscle function.

question: Thyroid gland secretes:
explanation:
• Thyroid secretes T4 and T3 (metabolism regulation). Also calcitonin.
• Iodine is essential for thyroid hormone synthesis.

question: Red blood cells are produced in:
explanation:
• RBCs (erythrocytes) are produced in red bone marrow.
• Erythropoietin from kidney stimulates production.

question: Normal adult pulse rate per minute is:
explanation:
• Normal adult pulse: 60-100/min. Bradycardia <60; tachycardia >100.
• Vital sign for nursing assessment.

question: Which cranial nerve is responsible for vision?
explanation:
• Optic nerve (II) carries visual information from retina to brain.
• Oculomotor (III) controls most eye movements.

question: Stomach pH is approximately:
explanation:
• Gastric acid creates pH 1.5-3.5. HCl and pepsin aid digestion.
• Mucus protects stomach lining.

question: Oxygen is transported in blood mainly bound to:
explanation:
• Hemoglobin in RBCs carries ~98% of O2 (oxyhemoglobin).
• Small amount dissolved in plasma.

question: Which is not a function of the liver?
explanation:
• Liver: bile, glycogen storage, detoxification, protein synthesis. Not primary blood filtration (kidney).
• Liver does filter portal blood.

question: Normal body temperature in Celsius is approximately:
explanation:
• Normal core temperature ~37°C (98.6°F). Fever >38°C.
• Vital sign in nursing.

question: Which hormone stimulates uterine contractions during labour?
explanation:
• Oxytocin from posterior pituitary stimulates uterine contractions and milk ejection.
• Used therapeutically for induction.

question: The small intestine is divided into:
explanation:
• Small intestine: duodenum, jejunum, ileum. Main site of absorption.
• Large intestine: cecum, colon, rectum.

question: Normal serum sodium range (mEq/L) is:
explanation:
• Normal Na+ 136-145 mEq/L. Hyponatremia <136; hypernatremia >145.
• Important in fluid balance and nursing care.

question: Which part of the brain controls breathing rate?
explanation:
• Medulla oblongata has respiratory centers (inspiration/expiration).
• Also controls heart rate, blood pressure.

question: Lymph nodes function in:
options: B. Immune response and filtration of lymph
explanation:
• Lymph nodes filter lymph and house lymphocytes (immune response).
• Part of lymphatic system.

question: Systolic blood pressure represents:
options: A. Pressure when heart is relaxed
B. Pressure when heart contracts (ventricular systole)
explanation:
• Systolic = pressure during ventricular contraction. Diastolic = during relaxation.
• Normal written as systolic/diastolic (e.g. 120/80).

question: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin with sunlight?
explanation:
• Vitamin D is synthesized in skin when exposed to UV light (7-dehydrocholesterol → cholecalciferol).
• Deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

question: The spinal cord extends from:
options: B. Medulla oblongata to approximately L1-L2
explanation:
• Spinal cord runs from medulla to about L1-L2 in adults. Below that is cauda equina.
• Protected by vertebral column.
